summary: This PR re-adopts PROJEXA's Permits/Drawings/Documents/Minutes-of-Meetings surface on top of a shared createDocumentRecord() upload helper, following the codebase's established reuse-the-documents-table pattern instead of adding new schema (no migrations touched, correctly tier1). Every new/changed route applies requireAuthOrApiKey plus requireRoleOrScope('member','write') on mutating endpoints, all reads/writes are properly tenant-scoped via withTenantContext(orgId), storage uploads use a randomized createId()-prefixed object path with a sanitized filename (no path traversal), signed URLs are short-lived (300s) generated server-side with the service-role client, and a new tenant-isolation test suite exercises the real service functions rather than just asserting a claim. No .github/workflows/** files are touched. The implementation is consistent, well-commented about its own scope boundaries, and matches prior sibling routes (permits/documents) closely enough to be low risk.
issues: The permits GET DTO renames the existing shipped field `expiryDate` to `endDate` (src/app/api/v1/projexa/permits/route.ts toPermitDto) — a breaking contract change for any existing consumer of this already-live v1 endpoint unless the PROJEXA client was updated in the same coordinated change; worth confirming before this ships to any external caller still expecting `expiryDate`.

`externalUrl` accepted on document/drawing creation (src/lib/services/document-service.ts createDocumentRecord, src/app/api/v1/projexa/drawings/route.ts) is stored and later returned verbatim as `documentUrl` with no scheme/format validation — a caller could store a non-http(s) URI (e.g. `javascript:`/`data:`) that a frontend consumer might later render as a clickable link; recommend restricting to http/https before storing.

src/lib/pdf/meeting-minutes-pdf.ts only checks for page overflow (`if (y > 700...)`) before the AI Summary and Action Items sections, not while rendering the Agenda or Minutes text blocks — a meeting with very long minutes/agenda text could render past the bottom of the page without a new page being added. Cosmetic, not a correctness/security blocker.
